To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) exercise reduces A1c levels, 2) exercise reduces adiposity, 3) exercise lowers triglycerides levels, 4) no research has definitvely proved a benefit of exerise on diabetes-related morbidity or mortality.
exercise is safe, effective, and beneficial for patients with type 1 or type 2 diabetes and that it should be prescribed for these patients as part of a comprehensive diabetes management plan.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of exercise on the metabolic control of diabetes.
the development of new exercise interventions to improve the health outcomes of patients with type 1 and type 2 diabetes.
the development of new and better drugs and therapies, the improvement of the quality of life for patients with diabetes, and the prevention of the complications of diabetes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
exercise reduces A1c, adiposity, triglycerides, and blood pressure, and that it improves cardiovascular fitness, insulin sensitivity, and quality of life.
regular physical activity is beneficial for the management of patients with type 1 or 2 diabetes.
exercise is beneficial in patients with type-2 diabetes, but the evidence for the benefit on patient-oriented outcomes is lacking.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
exercise is beneficial in patients with type 2 diabetes.
exercise has an important role in the management of type 2 diabetes.
regular exercise reduces the risk of diabetes complications, including cardiovascular disease and mortality.
The main takeaway from our work is that
exercise can help reduce the risk of type 2 diabetes and improve blood sugar control in people with diabetes.
exercise can be an effective tool in the treatment of type 2 diabetes, but that it is only one part of a multifaceted treatment plan.
we should not underestimate the potential of exercise to improve health.
